history_summary.value: The Pictave was developed from about 1900 by Raymond Lecointre near Poitiers from small European partridge-coloured bantam stock, and he used the hens to hatch and raise his pheasant chicks. It nearly went extinct after World War Two, and later cross-breeding to save it caused the breed to drift from its 1928 standard, prompting a 1998 effort to restore the original type.
